reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing the decision and canonical bytes, returned to the official 2026–2027 regulations and independently re-totalled Appendix I, checked the Year 2 selections by period, reconciled the concentration-preparation credit and verified the concentration and thesis entry rules. Reconsidered the actual UCR workbook content and terms and then checked the exact finished pair. This is a separate pass by the same AI.
findings: Appendix I and Article 4.6 give 60 EC in each year. Year 1 has eight 5 EC courses, four 2.5 EC skills courses, and two 5 EC projects. Year 2 uses the eight course and four skill slots from the Appendix I period lists plus Research Projects III and IV. The illustrated choice takes the first-listed Planetary Systems concentration, and Planetary Boundaries is its required preparation. Article 4.8(2) describes this as a skills course, but Appendix I places all three mandatory concentration preparations in the 5 EC course column, consistent with the separate 5 EC concentration preparation in Article 4.6. Year 3 uses four 5 EC courses, two 2.5 EC skills modules, one 5 EC design challenge and the 30 EC thesis. The table lists two courses and one skills unit in each concentration period. The example assigns skills credit to the third item in each period, consistent with the parallel Agricultural and Food skills labels. The official semester overview cautions that titles may change. No detailed syllabus claims are inferred from module titles.

Articles 4.9 and 5.2 require successful completion of the first-year core courses, skills and projects before concentration modules, and prior participation in the mandatory preparation with attendance met. Concentration registration is due before 1 June of the preceding academic year. Year 2 requires two courses and one skills module in each elective period, with eligibility subject to any catalogue prerequisites. The example selects coherent choices in the correct periods following the full first-year foundation. Article 5.3 requires an approved thesis plan before starting the final 30 EC individual project. The regulations describe no separately credited internship or extra thesis prerequisite within the standard plan.

The Ecology, Earth Systems and Life Science plan has direct course support and an explicit limitation in plant and food specialisation. Evolution is a direct academic addition. Both remaining offering conflicts were corrected, and the table identifies Maastricht’s distinct design and thesis components.
